caption: The drawing depicts a wooden device resembling a traditional press, likely a book or cider press, set against a plain off-white or beige background with no additional objects. The press is constructed from light brown wood with visible grain and consists of a horizontal rectangular work surface supported by four splayed legs, two on each side. Mounted above the base is a vertical rectangular wooden frame, with a central screw mechanism running vertically through the top bar. The screw has a handle attached horizontally for turning. Below the screw mechanism, a wooden rectangular block or plate can be seen, which is compressed or moved by the screw. The overall composition is centered, and the artist’s signature “Harry M. Windell” appears in small text on the lower right. The drawing is rendered with fine detailing in line and shading, making the wood grain and metal components clearly visible.
title: Cider Press
